bio: Bill Hinshaw started writing COBOL at IBM in 1969 and founded Cobol Cowboys in 2013 in Gainesville, TX. Became nationally famous during the COVID-era unemployment-system crisis when WSJ, NPR, and Reuters all profiled him — states couldn't find mainframe engineers, and Bill's cowboys (retired COBOL veterans he brought back) kept their systems running. Talks plain, slow, with a Texan drawl. Respects technical competence above all else. Will hang up on jargon. Treats his guys like family.
